risks.title: Dependence on Near-Term Refinancing
risks.score_rationale: Risk is central in the 10-K, with a 18-month loan of $530.8M due in December 2026. Language emphasizes the necessity to refinance before maturity. Capital category is heavily weighted. Risk is stable compared to prior year.

risks.title: Ability to Generate Operating Cash Flows
risks.score_rationale: The 10-K explicitly states that operating cash flows may be insufficient. Tone is cautious ('cannot assure'). Risk is repeated multiple times, indicating recurring concern. Capital category heavily impacted.

risks.title: Potential Shareholder Dilution
risks.score_rationale: Risk is mentioned as consequence of external financing need. Language is conditional ('if'). Less central than other liquidity risks, but linked to capitalization strategy.

risks.title: Debt Covenants and Restrictions
risks.score_rationale: Leverage ratio is constrained (3.5x, up to 4.0x for acquisitions). Compliance is confirmed, but consequences of breach would be severe. Precise and technical language, indicating a monitored risk.

risks.title: Costly Acquisitions Integration
risks.score_rationale: $1.7 billion spent on acquisitions in 2024. Risk relates to future capacity to integrate and fund such operations. Repeated mention in cash flows and obligations.

risks.title: Foreign Asset Repatriation Costs
risks.score_rationale: Tax risk on unrepatriated earnings is mentioned, with amount 'not readily determinable'. Less urgent, but potentially costly. Tax category, moderately weighted.

risks.title: Tax Obligations to Former Parent
risks.score_rationale: $51M in tax costs related to separation, of which $1.1M still owed. Transactional but contractual risk. Mention in near-term commitments.

ai_positioning.summary: RAL does not mention artificial intelligence (AI) or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing.
